dossier: A new biomedical study is being interpreted against a large prior literature, but the published report does not systematically place the new result against existing syntheses. The immediate scientific question is whether the apparent novelty or tension reflects what is already known.

admission_evidence.summary: Meta-research found systematic reviews were rarely used to contextualise new results; prior-evidence coverage is the corrective obligation.

dossier: An ecological dataset contains gaps in observations used for inference. Analyses can proceed by ignoring incomplete records, but the missing observations may alter estimated relationships and downstream conclusions.

admission_evidence.summary: The study shows ignoring missing data can distort inference and evaluates ways to recover information from incomplete observations.

dossier: A diagnostic-accuracy study applies the reference standard selectively rather than uniformly. The observed sample of verified results may therefore differ systematically from the population whose accuracy is being estimated.

admission_evidence.summary: Partial verification and test-result-based sampling bias diagnostic accuracy; this is an evaluator/measurement-design defect.

dossier: Biomedical animal studies often produce multiple outcomes, yet only part of the work becomes visible in publications. A reader trying to assess the evidence base cannot know whether unreported results materially change the scientific picture.

admission_evidence.summary: Interviews identify causes of incomplete results reporting; the immediate obligation is missing evidence availability rather than objective reformulation.

dossier: A pathology classifier encounters biopsy images from laboratories, scanners, or tissue conditions not represented in its training experience. Some predictions may therefore be unsupported even when the classifier appears confident.

admission_evidence.summary: External data outside training coverage caused unreliable predictions; conformal evidence coverage flags unsupported cases and systematic shifts.

dossier: Brain maps from different imaging resources are available, but they are expressed in disparate volumetric and surface coordinate systems. Direct comparison risks treating coordinate incompatibility as biological disagreement.

admission_evidence.summary: neuromaps provides transformations across coordinate systems to enable systematic comparison of brain maps.

dossier: An unsupervised representation learner optimizes a pretext task while downstream performance is the actual target. Continued improvement on the pretext objective can coincide with worsening target-task quality.

admission_evidence.summary: Controlled experiments isolate objective-function mismatch: optimizing the proxy/pretext objective can degrade the target.

dossier: Hydrographic observations use depth coordinates while an isopycnal ocean model is discretized by potential density. The same observations can be assimilated after translating innovations in different vertical coordinate spaces.

admission_evidence.summary: Experiments show vertical-coordinate choice changes assimilation accuracy; observation-space innovations improve multiple ocean fields.
